newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude business thins as prices edge up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude business thins as prices edge up.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices were notionally firmer Friday midday, but business had thinned out with an unexpected run-up in crude futures due to a gasoline play.
"Everyone wants to go into the weekend with flat positions," said a trader for a major oil company.
Trades through brokers were minimal and indications on differentials for the main traded domestic grades were little changed from late Thursday, with wider bid/off spreads.
A posted-plus trade was done at $1.85, with the August/September contango remaining steady at around 10/14 cents.
Light Louisian Sweet/St. James (LLS) looks to have peaked for now and was indicated at a 20/24 cents premium to benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI), traders said.

"Statoil (the Norwegian state oil company) are definitely working that ULCC (Ultra Large Crude Carrier) to the Gulf and that's helping to put a cap on LLS," said a trader at a large independent refiner.

Among other grades, Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was steady at either side of 30 cents under WTI; West Texas Sour/Midland was bid around $1.35 under WTI; Eugene Island was qouted at a wide margin of $1.50/$1.35 under and WTI/Midland was around 26/27 under.
